2. "Oh huh this place is weird" (falls into depression and/or mania)
3. "Get me out of here!" (moves away, often back to original city)

For the first few months, you will feel like you're living in paradise

But then you may have the creeping sense that something is off. I will spell them out for you because they took me a long time to fully notice:
↓
1922787848320589930 [2025-05-14] @TylerAlterman 💜 322 🔁 11
a. Flakiness
IME California culture is strong at *connecting* in the moment, but not showing up for one another when times get hard. People constantly maintain their optionality & cancel frequently. Everyone kinda just accepts this
https://t.co/dqPv2bA4r3
  [Quoting @TylerAlterman: SF & NY ppl mean something fundamentally different by “community”*  In SF it means that you will see the same ~100 ppl across a coliving house party, salon on utopian futures, burning man camp, psychedelic ceremony, and startup demo day  In NY it means that you have a small circle of friends you’ve known for years who will hold you in grief after your family member dies, help you move apartments, wingman for you, and drop Advil off at your office when you have a headache and can’t get out of meetings**  The SF type of community is way more accessible and flashy, which is why I got seduced by it for years. But the NY type of community has ultimately felt better for my soul  Footnotes: *this all is very specific to my demographic **this culture is less the case with the latest generation in NYC sadly, probably bc of covid]
↓
1922787849880973350 [2025-05-14] @TylerAlterman 💜 304 🔁 4
b. Lack of “realness”
There’s a sort of toxic positivity. Negative commentary is often a faux pas. Conflict aversion runs rampant, so people ghost each other instead of solving their tensions

What realness exists is often mediated through frameworks like "authentic relating"

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand represents a static **Aesthetic Appreciation** rather than an evolutionary narrative. The boundary object is California itself—its geography, weather, and natural beauty—which remains constant across four years (2021-2025). The discourse oscillates between pure celebration ("paradise on earth," "literally heaven") and Tyler Alterman's 2025 viral critique of California's social pathologies (flakiness, toxic positivity, spiritual hedonism). However, this dialectic does not produce synthesis or refinement; instead, it confirms a pre-existing duality: "California is physically beautiful but culturally hollow." The community does not evolve a new framework or social technology—they simply restate personal gratitude or warnings. High cohesion among repeat participants (brimmingvessel, vividvoid, TylerAlterman) but low knowledge production.

essential_tweets.annotation: The Thesis: Vividvoid's framing of California as 'paradise on earth' whose residents fail to appreciate it—sets up the central tension.
The Spiritual Charge: Vividvoid's hyperbolic call to 'throw yourself on the ground and weep'—establishes the tone of mystical reverence.
Personal Testimony: Brimmingvessel's autobiographical anchor ('moved here when i was 20')—validates California as a site of personal transformation.
The Viral Moment: Danielle Fong's 'california geography is overpowered'—condensing the aesthetic consensus into a meme-able phrase.
The Counter-Thesis: Tyler Alterman's thread opener introducing the 'California Curse'—pivoting from celebration to critique.
The Dialectic Setup: Tyler acknowledging California's undeniable physical beauty (with devil meme)—conceding the aesthetic point before attacking culture.
The Core Critique (Flakiness): Tyler's diagnosis of California's weak social fabric—the most-engaged point in his thread.
The Spiritual Hazard: Tyler naming 'narcissistic personal development' and 'spiritual hedonism'—articulating the shadow side of California's openness.
The Redemption Arc: Bumbadum's viral defense ('California is to be fought for')—reframing California as a contested civilizational project rather than abandoned ruin.
The Closing Image: Marvin's Yosemite photo ('california is literally heaven')—returning full circle to pure aesthetic worship, confirming the loop.
